layout.onthisday.dayBoundary.element: when the on-this-day set rolls over to the next date
layout.onthisday.dayBoundary.evidence: https://help.timehop.com/article/775-when-does-my-timehop-day-begin-and-end ('Your Timehop Day spans 24 hours from 5 am to 5 am')
layout.onthisday.dayBoundary.notes: Mechanics (not visual): Retro's Rewind is 'On this week' from the camera roll and shows no day boundary; the group's day still rolls over at 5 am group time (Timehop's documented day). Client passes p_local_date = date of (now in the group time zone minus 5 h) to on_this_day.

value.style: medium date (the locale's abbreviated month, day, year)

layout.onthisday.dateFormat.element: the memory's date shown as the display title over the photo (and in its accessibility label)
layout.onthisday.dateFormat.evidence: references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-b.jpg (RAW iOS 1260x2736, 3.000 px/pt, 420 pt wide) title 'Jul 22, 2022'; references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-a.png (RAW iOS 1320x2868, 3.000 px/pt, 440 pt wide) title 'May 1, 2019'; references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-panels.png (press render, Dec 2025) and references/auto/retro/store/retro-store-05.png (App Store render, 2.389 px/pt) 'July 5, 2021' (render)
layout.onthisday.dateFormat.method: read from the RAW captures; en-US medium date style prints 'Jul 22, 2022'
layout.onthisday.dateFormat.notes: RAW (Dec 2025) abbreviates the month; the store / press renders spell it out ('July 5, 2021'). RAW wins (R-* rule). Copy pattern retro.voice.formats.

color.onthisday.subtitle.element: subtitle under the date title ('On this day · {name}' / 'Memories · {name}'), over the photo
color.onthisday.subtitle.evidence: references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-panels.png (press render, Dec 2025) phone 1 'On this week' (x455-615, y450-490 px) and references/auto/retro/store/retro-store-05.png (App Store render, 2.389 px/pt) (x205-435, y850-895 px): glyph core (218,204,197) over the wall behind it (38-39,65-66,52)
color.onthisday.subtitle.method: alpha of white solved from the brightest 3 % of glyph pixels against the 30th-percentile background in the same box: R 0.83, G 0.73, B 0.71 → mean 0.76 = 0xC2
color.onthisday.subtitle.precision: ±0.06 alpha (the three channels disagree: the text may carry vibrancy over the photo)
color.onthisday.subtitle.notes: Retro draws the subtitle white at reduced opacity (components C-35 called it not measurable); this is the closest solve. Over the photo its contrast is photo-dependent (no top scrim in any capture).

dimension.onthisday.subtitleBaseline.evidence: references/auto/retro/store/retro-store-05.png (App Store render, 2.389 px/pt): '2021' digits y752-823 (baseline 823), 'On this week' 'O' y858-886 (baseline 886)
dimension.onthisday.subtitleBaseline.notes: The RAW captures show no subtitle (RWA has the expand chevron instead, RWB nothing); the press render and store render agree on the subtitle placement.

dimension.onthisday.dial.diameter.element: Rewind dial: outer diameter of the tick ring
dimension.onthisday.dial.diameter.evidence: references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-b.jpg (RAW iOS 1260x2736, 3.000 px/pt, 420 pt wide): centre (630, 2217.5); tick outer radius 225 px (p50 over 720 angles, design/research/retro-timehop.md) / 226.5 px (this pass, edge at 25 levels above the local background over 2880 angles)
dimension.onthisday.dial.diameter.notes: RWA (same month, larger phone) draws the ring smaller: outer radius 214.5 px = 143 pt, with a longer indicator (28 pt) and a larger play glyph — read as another state of the dial (it was not captured at rest); RWB's resting dial is used (MERGE RM-3). The store render ST-05 shows an earlier dial (≈133 pt, 9.8° pitch) — superseded by the RAW captures.

count.onthisday.dial.ticks.element: number of tick slots around the dial (long and short alternate)
count.onthisday.dial.ticks.evidence: references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-a.png (RAW iOS 1320x2868, 3.000 px/pt, 440 pt wide) centre (660, 2288.5) and references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-b.jpg (RAW iOS 1260x2736, 3.000 px/pt, 420 pt wide) centre (630, 2217.5): tick angles at a constant pitch 8.19° (25 + 26 consecutive ticks, ±0.07°)
count.onthisday.dial.ticks.method: background-subtracted polar profile (2880 angles, radius 100-300 px); 360° ÷ 8.19° = 43.96
count.onthisday.dial.ticks.notes: design/research/retro-timehop.md counted '≈45 (44/45)' by crossings; the pitch settles it at 44.

dimension.onthisday.dial.tickLong.element: long tick (even slots) length, measured from the ring's outer edge inward
dimension.onthisday.dial.tickLong.evidence: references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-b.jpg (RAW iOS 1260x2736, 3.000 px/pt, 420 pt wide) column x=638 across the 6 o'clock tick: ink y2384-2443 (partial pixels at both ends); polar profile inner radius 167 px vs outer 226.5 px; references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-a.png (RAW iOS 1320x2868, 3.000 px/pt, 440 pt wide) 155.5 → 214.5 px
dimension.onthisday.dial.tickLong.method: ink length incl. partial-pixel coverage ÷ 3; RWA and RWB agree (59-59.5 px)
dimension.onthisday.dial.tickLong.notes: design/research/retro-timehop.md gives 18 from the 50th-percentile inner radius over all angles (171 px); this pass measured the ticks themselves.

dimension.onthisday.dial.tickShort.element: short tick (odd slots) length, from the ring's outer edge inward
dimension.onthisday.dial.tickShort.evidence: references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-b.jpg (RAW iOS 1260x2736, 3.000 px/pt, 420 pt wide) polar profile: short ticks inner radius 191 px, outer 226.5 px; references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-a.png (RAW iOS 1320x2868, 3.000 px/pt, 440 pt wide): 179.5 → 214.5 px

dimension.onthisday.dial.tickWidth.element: width (stroke) of every tick and of the indicator
dimension.onthisday.dial.tickWidth.evidence: references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-a.png (RAW iOS 1320x2868, 3.000 px/pt, 440 pt wide) row y=2488 across the 6 o'clock tick: x663-672 full (129) + partial 96 / 107 over background 75 (≈9.9 px); indicator at 6°: 9.5 px across; references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-b.jpg (RAW iOS 1260x2736, 3.000 px/pt, 420 pt wide) row y=2415: 8 full + 2 partial (≈9 px), indicator rows 2220-2229 (10 px)
dimension.onthisday.dial.tickWidth.notes: Ends look square at this scale (the long-tick column starts with one partial pixel); a round cap of 1.6 pt cannot be ruled out.

color.onthisday.dial.tick.element: dial ticks (all slots except the indicator)
color.onthisday.dial.tick.evidence: references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-a.png (RAW iOS 1320x2868, 3.000 px/pt, 440 pt wide): 26 ticks at radius 200 px, peak vs the background half a pitch either side, e.g. (157,147,138) over (114,100,87), (134,128,120) over (83,73,62); references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-b.jpg (RAW iOS 1260x2736, 3.000 px/pt, 420 pt wide) (JPEG): 7 ticks, alpha 0.30-0.33
color.onthisday.dial.tick.method: alpha of white per channel = (peak − bg) ÷ (255 − bg); RWA median 0.300 (all channels 0.295-0.307 on the ticks away from the share circle) = 0x4D
color.onthisday.dial.tick.notes: Same value as color.global.textTertiary dark and APK white @ 0.3 (Retro's alpha table, RP §3.3); kept as its own token because its role is the dial on media in both appearances.

dimension.onthisday.dial.indicatorLength.element: indicator (the current memory's slot): solid tick from the ring's outer edge inward
dimension.onthisday.dial.indicatorLength.evidence: references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-b.jpg (RAW iOS 1260x2736, 3.000 px/pt, 420 pt wide): indicator at 178° (9 o'clock), row y=2224 white (255) from x404 to x453.5 → radius 176.5-226 px; references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-a.png (RAW iOS 1320x2868, 3.000 px/pt, 440 pt wide): indicator at 6° from radius 130 to 214 px (28 pt)
dimension.onthisday.dial.indicatorLength.notes: Colour = color.global.textOnMedia (both captures read 255). RWA's 28-pt indicator goes with its smaller ring (another state, see dimension.onthisday.dial.diameter). Capture that would settle the states: 10 s screen recording of the Rewind dial dragged and released.

dimension.onthisday.dial.glyph.element: play / pause glyph in the dial centre: ink height
dimension.onthisday.dial.glyph.evidence: references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-b.jpg (RAW iOS 1260x2736, 3.000 px/pt, 420 pt wide): play triangle ink x589-683, y2165-2269 (31.7 × 35.0 pt); references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-a.png (RAW iOS 1320x2868, 3.000 px/pt, 440 pt wide): x616-716, y2233-2344 (33.7 × 37.3 pt)
dimension.onthisday.dial.glyph.method: bounding box of pixels > 245 ÷ 3; RWB (dial at rest) used
dimension.onthisday.dial.glyph.notes: Glyphs icon.global.play / icon.global.pause (fill variant = a state, icon.global.variantRule), colour color.global.textOnMedia; size the symbol so its ink is this tall.

value.angleReference: measured clockwise from 3 o'clock (screen y grows downward)
value.indicator: drawn on the current memory's slot instead of that slot's tick
value.step: one slot per memory; dragging around the centre moves one memory per slot crossed; clockwise = next (older), counter-clockwise = previous
value.playback: while playing, the indicator moves one slot each time the memory changes
value.haptic: haptic.global.select once per slot crossed (and per automatic step while playing)

layout.onthisday.dial.evidence: references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-a.png (RAW iOS 1320x2868, 3.000 px/pt, 440 pt wide): ticks at 6.0° + k × 8.19°, indicator on slot 0 (6.0°), long ticks at 22.4°, 38.8° … (even); references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-b.jpg (RAW iOS 1260x2736, 3.000 px/pt, 420 pt wide): ticks at 5.7° + k × 8.19°, indicator on slot 21 (178.1°), long ticks even; references/auto/retro/apk/retro-android-2026.10.1150-strings.txt rewind_home_nux_message ('Drag the dial to take a spin through your memories.'); references/auto/retro/apk/retro-android-2026.10.1150-excerpts.txt 'w9e.java (Rewind tab …) collects a flow with new lh2(view, i) => tick haptic per dial step'
layout.onthisday.dial.method: polar profile of both RAW captures; behaviour from Retro's own NUX string and package (one tick per dial step)
layout.onthisday.dial.notes: Inferred, not observed directly: that the indicator marks the current memory and starts on slot 0 (RWA shows slot 0, RWB slot 21, TC-RWP renders other slots) and that clockwise means forward (clock convention). A 10 s recording of the dial being dragged closes both (MERGE RM-4).

dimension.onthisday.controls.centerY.element: dial centre (and the centres of the share / random circles) above the safe-area bottom
dimension.onthisday.controls.centerY.evidence: references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-b.jpg (RAW iOS 1260x2736, 3.000 px/pt, 420 pt wide): dial centre y=2217.5 px = 739.2 pt on a 912-pt screen; safe-area bottom 878 pt (34-pt home-indicator inset); share circle y-centre 2217 (x107-299); references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-a.png (RAW iOS 1320x2868, 3.000 px/pt, 440 pt wide): centre 762.8 pt on a 956-pt screen → 159.2 pt above its safe-area bottom
dimension.onthisday.controls.centerY.precision: ±0.5 pt (RWB); RWA differs by 20 pt (another dial state, MERGE RM-3)
dimension.onthisday.controls.centerY.notes: In Retro the tab bar sits between the dial and the home indicator; our page has no tab bar, and the controls keep Retro's distance from the bottom so the photo is framed the same way.

value.arrangement: equal gaps across the screen width: edge | share | dial | random | edge (the dial's box = dimension.onthisday.dial.diameter)
value.circles: size.global.circleButtonLarge, fill color.global.glass, glyphs icon.global.share / icon.global.random in a size.global.icon box, color.global.textOnMedia
value.playing: share and random hidden (fade duration.global.fade, easing.global.standard); the dial shows icon.global.pause

layout.onthisday.controls.element: bottom control row of the Rewind page
layout.onthisday.controls.evidence: references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-b.jpg (RAW iOS 1260x2736, 3.000 px/pt, 420 pt wide): share x107-299, dial ticks 403.5-856.5, random x959-1151 on 1260 px → gaps 35.7 / 34.8 / 34.8 / 35.7 pt; references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-device-a.png (RAW iOS 1320x2868, 3.000 px/pt, 440 pt wide): share x118.5-310.5, random x1009.5-1201.5 on 1320 px → edge gaps 39.5 pt, circle → 150-pt dial box 41 pt; references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-panels.png (press render, Dec 2025) phone 1 and references/auto/retro/store/retro-store-05.png (App Store render, 2.389 px/pt): playing (pause glyph) with no share / random circles; references/auto/retro/press/tc-2025-12-rewind-panels.png (press render, Dec 2025) phone 2: paused (play glyph) with both circles
layout.onthisday.controls.method: edge runs on the circle row (luminance step ≥ 6); equal-gap model fits both RAW captures within 1.5 pt
layout.onthisday.controls.notes: Share / random glyph ink measures 19.7 × 24.7 and 23.7 × 23.3 pt on RWB, inside the 24-pt glyph box.

duration.onthisday.memoryChange.element: cross-fade from one memory to the next while playing (automatic advance)
duration.onthisday.memoryChange.evidence: https://static.vidday.com/vidday_theme_samples/theme_happy_birthday.mp4 (listed on https://www.vidday.com/examples; 1920x1080, 30 fps, 135.72 s); per-frame diff references/auto/vidday/frames/vidday-theme-happy-birthday-framediff.csv: photo-to-photo crossfades 23.233-23.933, 26.467-27.167, 30.467-31.167, 64.133-64.833, 68.167-68.867, 80.500-81.200, 92.133-92.833 s (21-22 changed frames each)
duration.onthisday.memoryChange.method: first to last changed frame of each crossfade (mean abs grey diff > 0.8 on a 192-px decode), 30 fps
duration.onthisday.memoryChange.notes: Mechanics (memory montage, VidDay; MERGE G2-17): Retro's own photo change was not captured (Fast Company: photos 'flip by', text only). A step made by dragging the dial cross-fades over duration.global.crossfade (100 ms, Retro) instead, so scrubbing keeps up with the finger. Reduce Motion: the cross-fade stays (it is already the substitute, layout.global.reduceMotion).
duration.onthisday.memoryChange.precision: ±33 ms (1 frame); curve not measurable (duration only)

duration.onthisday.playHold.element: time one memory stays on screen while the dial is playing, before the next one
duration.onthisday.playHold.evidence: references/auto/vidday/help/vidday-help-display-length-2025-02-07.png (https://help.vidday.com/can-i-change-the-display-length-on-photos-and-text-cards/, last update 07.02.2025: 'Photos and text cards will automatically be set to display for 4 seconds by default.'); measured in https://static.vidday.com/vidday_theme_samples/theme_happy_birthday.mp4 (listed on https://www.vidday.com/examples; 1920x1080, 30 fps, 135.72 s) (references/auto/vidday/frames/vidday-theme-happy-birthday-framediff.csv): text-card and photo slots start-to-start 4.033 s (title 2.967 -> 7.000), 4.000-4.067 s (photos 26.467 -> 30.467 -> 34.533, 64.133 -> 68.167 -> 72.200, 92.133 -> 96.133), 4.000 s (end text card 128.700 -> 132.700)
duration.onthisday.playHold.method: documented default, confirmed by the slot pitch in the sample render (frame diff, 30 fps)
duration.onthisday.playHold.notes: Mechanics: Retro's play cadence was not captured; the same documented per-photo time as the year story (duration.year.story.card, MERGE G2-18). Playing stops after the last memory (the dial shows play again).

easing.year.story.reveal.element: curve of the headline / subline reveal
easing.year.story.reveal.evidence: references/auto/wrapped/frames/wrapped24-rec-emilycraig-reveal-positions.csv (25 headline positions at 30 fps, 15.533-16.333 s, y956 -> 916 px); fit: references/auto/wrapped/frames/wrapped24-rec-emilycraig-reveal-fit.csv
easing.year.story.reveal.method: least-squares cubic Bezier over all 25 samples (0.05 grid, then 0.01 grid): rms 0.012 of the travel = 0.48 px, below the 1-px quantization
easing.year.story.reveal.notes: Gap fill (MERGE G2-19). This is the headline's curve (duration.year.story.reveal.headline 800 ms, dimension .headlineShift). The subline follows a different, decelerating curve: easing.year.story.reveal.subline (new token). No single curve fits both (best joint fit rms 0.12 = 5-7 px). The earlier 'not fitted' note used only the three summary points (layout.year.story.reveal.samples). Documented curves tried: FastOutSlowIn (0.4,0,0.2,1) rms 0.060, easeInOut 0.112. Mechanics kept from Spotify Wrapped (year-story pacing; docs/REDESIGN_BRIEF.md): applies to the headline / subline of text cards inside the frame. Reduce Motion: cross-fade of the same durations (layout.global.reduceMotion).
easing.year.story.reveal.precision: ±0.05 per control point (flat error surface); residual 0.5 px

easing.year.story.reveal.subline.element: curve of the subline rising in (with duration.year.story.reveal.subline, .sublineDelay, dimension .sublineOffset)
easing.year.story.reveal.subline.evidence: references/auto/wrapped/frames/wrapped24-rec-emilycraig-reveal-positions.csv (19 subline positions at 30 fps, 15.800-16.400 s, y1083 -> 1028 px); fit: references/auto/wrapped/frames/wrapped24-rec-emilycraig-reveal-fit.csv
easing.year.story.reveal.subline.method: least-squares cubic Bezier over all 19 samples (0.05 grid, then 0.01 grid): rms 0.008 of the travel = 0.46 px
easing.year.story.reveal.subline.notes: Added in the gap-fill pass (MERGE G2-19) next to easing.year.story.reveal (headline). Closest documented curve: M3 standard decelerate (0,0,0,1), rms 0.047. Reduce Motion: cross-fade with the same durations (layout.global.reduceMotion). Mechanics kept from Spotify Wrapped (year-story pacing; docs/REDESIGN_BRIEF.md): applies to the headline / subline of text cards inside the frame. Reduce Motion: cross-fade of the same durations (layout.global.reduceMotion).
